quote: Gordon Royle found the first handful of 17-clue puzzles on a Japanese-language website in early 2005, beginning systematic research into minimal Sudoku puzzles
note: This is a sub-case of the Sudoku problem. The minimal puzzle problem has no single attributed originator and emerged organically as Sudoku gained global popularity (2004-2005). Gordon Royle's pioneering empirical work on 17-clue puzzles in early 2005 marks the emergence of this as an active research question. The first formal academic treatment was Herzberg and Murty (2007) in Notices of the American Mathematical Society. Dating to 2005 reflects the emergence of the problem through Royle's work rather than a formal pose.
